successors.name: Landgraviate of Hesse-Darmstadt
successors.text: the Bergstrasse and the Main lands below Frankfurt, 'to Hesse-Darmstadt and the Nassau princes'

successors.name: County of Nassau
successors.text: the Rheingau, Höchst, Königstein, Cronberg and Lahnstein to Nassau-Usingen (Duchy of Nassau page)

successors.name: Kingdom of Prussia
successors.text: 'Eichsfeld and Erfurt to the Kingdom of Prussia'

successors.name: Principality of Aschaffenburg
successors.text: 'Dalberg kept the Aschaffenburg area as a principality'; the elector's seat 'was moved to Regensburg'

ledger.x: 780: Mainz gains territory and is raised to archbishopric.
1022: the archbishopric lists its Eichsfeld possessions.
28 October 1462: Adolf of Nassau takes Mainz.
October 1463: the Treaty of Zeilsheim ends the Diocesan Feud.
By 1581 the County of Königstein belongs to the Electorate: 'By 1581, Königstein belonged to the Electorate of Mainz'.

21 October 1792: Custine's French army occupies Mainz ('occupied Mainz on 21 October 1792'); the Free State proclaimed on 18 March 1793 ('Rhenish-German National Convention', Republic of Mainz) extended to Bingen in the west and Landau in the south.
22 July 1793: Prussian and Austrian troops retake Mainz ('conquered the city on 22 July 1793').
1795: the French hold Mainz again ('in 1795 when Mainz came under French control again').
9 February 1801: the occupation ends in annexation at Lunéville.
1801: the left bank goes to France.
1803: the Rheingau and the Taunus-side lordships go to Nassau-Usingen.
1803: 'its right bank areas along the Main below Frankfurt to Hesse-Darmstadt and the Nassau princes'.

1803: the Electorate of Mainz ends in the German mediatisation; 'In 1802, Mainz lost its archiepiscopal character'; Dalberg's seat moved to Regensburg, and his Aschaffenburg principality became the Grand Duchy of Frankfurt in 1810.

wars.name: Mainz Diocesan Feud
wars.outcome: Adolf of Nassau wins; the Treaty of Zeilsheim (October 1463) gives castles and towns to the Palatinate, Hesse and briefly Saxony, and Diether a small principality (Höchst, Steinheim, Dieburg).

wars.name: French Revolutionary Wars (Mainz)
wars.outcome: France occupies Mainz in 1792, loses it on 22 July 1793, holds it from 1795; the left bank is lost in 1801.

certainty.note: The pages give no boundaries; the Electorate was a set of non-contiguous blocks (Rhine, Main, Eichsfeld, Erfurt).
